newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - July 8.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
CHINA TIMES - Taiwan may allow mainland China-funded businesses to enter the island after Taiwan joins World Trade Organisation.
Ruling Nationalist Party suppresses internal resistance to revise constitution.

UNITED DAILY NEWS - Ruling Nationalist Party suspends party rights of national assemblyman Lu Hsueh-chang for two years as Lu refuses to back the party's proposal to freeze all provincial-level elections.
Taiwan tourists, executives trapped in Cambodia.
LIBERTY TIMES - Southern Tainan Science-based Park preparatory committee starts operations.
Schools to implement two-day weekend every other week from next year.
COMMERCIAL TIMES - Insider trading will be treated as major economic crime.
Taiwan's trade deficit with Japan rises.
ECONOMIC DAILY NEWS - Central bank on Monday absorbs T$26 billion in funds from banking system.
Finance Ministry considers lowering criteria for major shareholders' stock ownership.
